newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, nearbys down with beef.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, nearbys down with beef.

text.p: Weakness in wholesale beef prices weighed on nearby CME live cattle futures and prices finished mostly lower, traders said. Feeders ended higher as corn futures turned lower late, traders said.
October live cattle fell late following further losses in boxed beef values before again rebounding somewhat on underlying support from tight fed cattle supplies, traders said.
Boxed beef values dipped to lowest levels in 1-1/2 weeks, prompting wire house and local selling. Sell stops added to losses before short covering pared losses, they said.

Underlying support continued to reflect the tight fed cattle situation. Reduced cattle placements earlier in the year tightened current available fat cattle supplies. Showlists are expected to continue easing into September or later before rising later in the fall, they said.

RBH, Refco and R.J. O'Brien notably sold early before local short covering and scattered commission house buying lent support. R.J. O'Brien bought on the recovery before selling by Lind-Waldock, Saul Stone and locals took futures down into sell stops. Buying was scattered at the close, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, volatility was steady to weak. There was some small hedging interest in back months early, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures generally followed the lead of live cattle but recovered late when corn futures fell, traders said.

Smith Barney bought October late. E.D.& F. Man sold most of the session and spreaders were on both sides of October feeder cattle/October live cattle. Merrill Lynch, Lind-Waldock and LIT division of First Options were early sellers in October, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.06 at $63.22 per cwt, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.225 cent lower to 0.075 higher with October off most at 71.500 cents per lb. Feeders ended 0.050 cent lower to 0.200 higher with October up 0.100 at 63.125 cents.
